chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so fresh dates were brought to him. He began eating from them and drinking water, and he handed me the bowl. I disliked returning it, so I drank until he did that repeatedly.

He said, so I said: 'I used to have excess phlegm, so I complained about it to Ahran, the physician of Al-Hajjaj.' He said to me: 'Do you have a palm tree in your orchard?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Are there palm trees in it?' I said: 'Yes.' So he said to me: 'Count for me what is in it.'

So I counted until I reached Al-Hayrun (a type of date). He said to me: 'Eat seven of them whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink water.' So I did that, and I wanted to spit but I was unable to do so. So I complained to him about that, so he said to me: 'Drink a little water and hold back until your constitution becomes balanced.'
So I did that. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'As for me, had it not been for the water, I would not care if I did not taste it.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam al-Sadiq

ai.seo_question: What is the medical and spiritual benefit of eating dates with water according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia tradition of *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the physiological benefits of consuming fresh dates (*rutab*) with water to balance the body's humors. The narrative highlights a practical medical anecdote regarding the treatment of excess phlegm, demonstrating how dietary adjustments can restore constitutional equilibrium, while the Imam’s personal preference underscores the spiritual and physical purity associated with this Sunnah. It serves as a key reference for understanding the interplay between physical health and spiritual discipline in Shia jurisprudence and medicine.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Ammar Al Sabaty who said,

‘I was with Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> brought me some dates, and he<sup>asws</sup> went on to eat from it, and drank the water, and he<sup>asws</sup> gave me the bowl. So I disliked to return it, so I drank until I had done that repeatedly.

So I said, ‘I was with excess phlegm so I complained about it to Ahran the physician of Al-Hajjaj’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Is there a palm tree for you in the orchard?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Therein are palm trees?’ I said, ‘Yes’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Count to me<sup>asws</sup> whatever its therein’.

So I counted until I reached Al-Heyroun (a type of date). So heasws said to me: ‘Eat seven dates from it whenever you intend to sleep, and do not drink the water’. So I did it, and I wanted to spit but I did not have the ability upon that. So I complained to himasws of that, so heasws said to me: ‘Drink the water, a little, and wait until your condition is moderate’.
So I did it. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for myself<sup>asws</sup>, so had it not been for the water, I would not care if I<sup>asws</sup> do not taste it’.
en.sarwar: 18. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah ibn Maymun from ‘Ammar al-Sabatiy who has said the following:

“I once was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when fresh dates were brought. He (the Imam) began to eat, drink water and gave to me the bowl of water and I disliked to decline. Therefore, I drank until he (the Imam) did it several times.

I then said, ‘I experience increased phlegm, and I complained about it before Ahran, the physician of al-Hajjaj and he asked me, “Do you have palm trees in the garden?” I replied, “Yes, there are.” He asked me to name them and I named until I mentioned al- Hirun (a certain tree) and he said, “Eat seven dates thereof when going to bed and do not drink water.”

I followed his instruction and I did not have any moisture in my mouth to spit. I complained before him and he said drink a small amount of water and hold back from drinking more until your condition is balanced.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I without water do not even mind if I did not taste it.’”
